title: HealthLine - SOC 2 / ISO 27001 Posture Review
summary: Redwood walked HealthLine security and compliance team through SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture, Trust Center access, control mappings, SSO/RBAC, audit log retention, and KMS/encryption options. Agreed next steps: share SOC2 + ISO reports, grant Trust Center read-only access, run a control-mapping workshop, and schedule dedicated private deployment scoping if needed.
next_steps: Priya to share SOC 2 Type II and latest ISO attestation - by 2025-06-12
Grant HealthLine read-only access to Redwood Trust Center (link) - by 2025-06-13
Schedule 90m controls-mapping workshop with Security + Compliance - target week of 2025-06-16
Marco to prepare architecture diagram and KMS integration options - by 2025-06-15
Lena to confirm procurement timeline and required artifacts - by 2025-06-20
action_items: Priya Shah | Share SOC 2 Type II report and ISO attestation (redacted) | 2025-06-12
Redwood Trust Center Admin | Invite HealthLine security users (read-only) | 2025-06-13
Marco Diaz | Prepare controls mapping spreadsheet for HealthLine -- include mapping to NIST 800-53 & ISO 27002 | 2025-06-15
Amit Verma (HealthLine) | Send list of regulator-required controls for residency | 2025-06-14
transcript:
[00:00] Priya Shah: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you taking the time. I'm Priya, account lead for HealthLine. With me is Marco from Solutions Engineering and Elise from Customer Success.
[00:12] Marta Lopez: Hi, Marta here, CISO at HealthLine. We'll kick off with our posture questions around SOC 2 and ISO.
[00:17] Tom Reeves: Tom as well, head of IT -- we'll want details on logs, retention, and residency.
[00:23] Priya Shah: Great -- high level agenda is SOC 2/ISO artifacts, Trust Center access, controls mapping, and then a deep dive on encryption, KMS and SSO. Marco will drive the tech bits.
[00:31] Marco Diaz: Hey all -- quick note, transcription might show some words weirdly, I think I heard someone say KV cash earlier, it's KV cache.
[00:37] Jing Zhao: Yep, no problem, happy to correct on the fly.
[00:40] Marco Diaz: Cool. So starting with reports, Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II covering availability, security and confidentiality for our hosted and dedicated offerings -- we also have an ISO 27001 certificate and associated Statement of Applicability. The most recent SOC 2 engagement period is Jan- Dec 2024.
[00:56] Marta Lopez: Do you provide the full SOC 2 Type II report or an AICPA redacted report? Our legal team needs assertion plus auditor's testing evidence.
[01:04] Priya Shah: We can share the SOC 2 Type II report with standard redactions -- auditor details and testing procedures are included. For more granular mappings, Marco can provide the controls mapping spreadsheet that aligns Redwood controls to common frameworks.
[01:16] Marco Diaz: Right -- we maintain a controls matrix mapping Redwood controls to SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria, ISO 27001 Annex A, and NIST. It's typically a spreadsheet we review during the workshop.
[01:25] Amit Verma: Is that the same matrix you use for customers or do you produce a bespoke mapping? Some of our regulators require a specific mapping.
[01:32] Marco Diaz: We have a canonical mapping and then we add a custom column during workshops to show where controls satisfy specific regulator needs. So we can do that for HealthLine.
[01:41] Lena Ortiz: On Trust Center access -- what exactly is in there? We need evidence like policy docs, encryption key handling, and incident timelines.
[01:48] Priya Shah: Trust Center contains the SOC 2 and ISO artifacts (redacted), our security policies, penetration test summaries, vulnerability management process, incident response report templates, and audit log retention details. We can grant read-only user accounts for your security team.
[02:01] Tom Reeves: What about audit logs -- how long do we retain admin/audit logs and can we export them to our SIEM?
[02:08] Marco Diaz: By default audit logs are retained for 90 days in the hosted offering. We support export via secure S3 export or direct SIEM integration; for Dedicated or Private deployments you can configure retention to meet your policy, and we can stream logs to your log collector.
[02:24] Jing Zhao: When you say S3 export is that encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys?
[02:30] Marco Diaz: Exports are encrypted in transit and at rest. For hosting we use Redwood-managed keys by default, but you can opt for KMS integration -- we support AWS KMS customer-managed keys for hosted customers and HSM integrations for Private deployments.
[02:45] Marta Lopez: Do you provide key rotation policies and access controls for keys? We require a documented rotation schedule and separation of duties.
[02:52] Marco Diaz: Yes, we document rotation cadence; with customer-managed KMS the rotation is controlled by you. For Redwood-managed keys we rotate per industry best practices and store rotation logs in our key management audit trail.
[03:02] Tom Reeves: We need RBAC granularities -- can you show us role definitions and support SCIM for provisioning?
[03:08] Priya Shah: Redwood supports SSO via SAML 2.0 and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC includes predefined roles (admin, developer, read-only-security) and custom roles if you need narrower permission sets.
[03:18] Jing Zhao: Is there an approval workflow for privilege escalation?
[03:21] Marco Diaz: There's an elevate-to-admin flow and we can integrate with your ticketing system for approvals; right now it's configurable per deployment.
[03:29] Marta Lopez: For ISO we need evidence of risk assessment and treatment logs -- do you keep artefacts showing risk register changes over time?
[03:36] Marco Diaz: We maintain a risk register and show quarterly risk assessments; excerpts are included in Trust Center. For full evidence we can arrange a controlled review during the mapping workshop.
[03:45] Amit Verma: Data residency -- our patients are EU-based, we need EU data storage and processing controls. Do you support region isolation?
[03:52] Priya Shah: Yes -- Redwood hosts in multiple regions. For Hosted we can pin workloads to EU regions; Dedicated gives physical isolation on GPU pools, and Private deployment gives you full on-prem/VPC control. We also have contract language for data residency in our DPA.
[04:07] Tom Reeves: How does fallback and cross-region replication work? If you pin to EU, is there automatic failover to US which could violate residency?
[04:15] Marco Diaz: Failover is policy driven -- for residency-sensitive customers we configure region-affinity and disable cross-region backups. There are also controls for manual disaster recovery that meet residency constraints.
[04:26] Lena Ortiz: About penetration tests -- can you share the last external pentest results and remediation timeline?
[04:32] Priya Shah: We publish pentest summaries in Trust Center and can provide detailed remediation reports under NDA. Our last external pentest was March 2025, and the high/medium findings were remediated within our SLA timeframe.
[04:44] Marta Lopez: For SOC 2 testing, do you have evidence for vulnerability scanning frequency and patching windows?
[04:50] Marco Diaz: Yes -- vulnerability scans run weekly, critical/urgent patches are applied within our emergency change window, normally 72 hours for critical. Details and evidence are in the SOC 2 testing documentation.
[04:59] Jing Zhao: One of our compliance folks asked about segmented network controls -- how do you separate customer workloads on shared infra?
[05:06] Marco Diaz: We use a multi-tenant model with tenant isolation at the orchestration layer, strict namespace segmentation, and kernel hardening. For Dedicated you get separate GPU pools and network isolation. For Private you get full separation.
[05:20] Tom Reeves: Are there any third-party subprocessors we should know about? Our policy requires a list and subprocessor agreements.
[05:27] Priya Shah: Absolutely -- Trust Center has our subprocessor list. We have DPA language and subprocessors are contractually bound to the same security requirements.
[05:36] Marta Lopez: Audit logs -- can we get immutable logs for the entire audit trail and a tamper-evident mechanism?
[05:42] Marco Diaz: We support append-only logs with write-once retention for critical events and can provide signed log digests for tamper evidence. For the highest assurance we recommend Dedicated or Private mode where you control the retention store.
[05:55] Amit Verma: Concerning encryption in transit -- do you use mTLS between services?
[05:59] Marco Diaz: Yes, internal services use mTLS; all external traffic is TLS 1.2+ (we recommend 1.3).
[06:05] Lena Ortiz: Is Redwood willing to put specific security SLAs in contract for incident response times and notification windows?
[06:11] Priya Shah: Yes -- for enterprise contracts we include incident response SLAs, notification timelines (e.g., 72-hour initial notification) and escalation contacts. We can surface standard SLA language and negotiate specifics.
[06:20] Tom Reeves: If we opt for Private deployment, what parts of the control set remain with us vs Redwood? We need a clear shared responsibility matrix.
[06:28] Marco Diaz: We'll generate a shared responsibility matrix. Typically Redwood handles the runtime, model binaries, and the control plane unless you choose air-gapped on-prem where you take more responsibility for infrastructure and keys.
[06:40] Priya Shah: Quick note -- we'll include that matrix in the controls-mapping workshop packet.
[06:45] Marco Diaz: On KMS integration specifics: for AWS KMS we support AWS-encrypted S3 with CMKs, and we present options for envelope encryption. For customers using Azure or GCP we can integrate with their KMS equivalents for Dedicated and Private.
[06:59] Jing Zhao: Do you have guidance for BYOK vs Redwood-managed keys in terms of operational burden?
[07:05] Marco Diaz: BYOK (customer-managed) gives you maximum control but you manage rotation and key lifecycle; Redwood-managed reduces burden but requires trust in our key ops and rotation logs. We'll provide runbooks for either approach.
[07:18] Priya Shah: A quick pause -- Marta, anything from legal you want us to call out?
[07:22] Marta Lopez: We will need to review the redacted SOC 2 and the ISO attestation, and we also want the controls mapping to show where certain data residency and encryption controls are implemented so our auditors can tick boxes.
[07:33] Priya Shah: Understood. We usually do a dedicated 90-minute workshop for that. Marco will lead the controls mapping and we'll bring Security + Product.
[07:42] Marco Diaz: We'll also prepare a sample control evidence package for two or three representative controls -- e.g., access control, encryption key management, incident response -- so auditors can spot-check.
[07:52] Tom Reeves: For automation -- can we automate evidence pulls? It'd be great if we could pull log excerpts and key rotation history via API.
[07:59] Marco Diaz: We have APIs for audit logs and certain metadata; for more sensitive evidence we do controlled exports. We'll detail available endpoints in the follow-up doc.
[08:09] Amit Verma: Do you support periodic independent audits on customer-specific deployments? For Dedicated we might request an annual audit.
[08:16] Priya Shah: Yes -- we accommodate audit requests for Dedicated and Private deployments; we'll coordinate scope and NDA as needed.
[08:25] Lena Ortiz: Regarding procurement timeline, we aim to finalize vendor selection by end of Q3. We'll need pricing and the contract SLRs.
[08:33] Priya Shah: We'll send pricing for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options and include security annex language.
[08:40] Marco Diaz: One technical detail I want to mention -- KV cache persistence and model artifacts are treated as ephemeral in hosted mode unless customers enable long-term storage; we can show artifact lifecycle during the workshop.
[08:52] Jing Zhao: Are model weights ever stored outside the region?
[08:55] Marco Diaz: No -- weights for region-pinned deployments remain in-region. Non-pinned workloads may be replicated for performance.
[09:02] Marta Lopez: For ISO evidence we need to see policy change logs and training records. Do you store training completion data for staff?
[09:09] Marco Diaz: Yes -- we keep training records and the HR/Training evidence is available in Trust Center summaries; detailed records can be shared under NDA.
[09:18] Priya Shah: Ok -- wrapping toward next steps. We'll: share SOC 2 and ISO redacted reports, invite you to Trust Center, prepare controls mapping and a workshop, and provide KMS integration options. Any blockers?
[09:29] Marta Lopez: No blockers. One ask -- can you include explicit examples showing how Redwood meets our regulator clause on crypto-agility?
[09:36] Marco Diaz: We'll add a crypto-agility appendix -- rotation, algorithm deprecation, and fallback guidance.
[09:42] Tom Reeves: Also please include SIEM integration sample config for Splunk and Datadog.
[09:47] Marco Diaz: Will do.
[09:50] Lena Ortiz: We'll expect the docs by Friday. Procurement will review and come back with any contract changes.
[09:55] Priya Shah: Great -- we'll follow up. Thanks everyone.
[09:58] (crosstalk / meeting ends)
